output.methodChoice: C+D: Kepner-Tregoe IS/IS NOT across sites, plus competing-hypotheses elimination, since site-level comparison discriminates the rivals.
output.brief: The evidence points to a combination, not RotaWeave alone. The basic app tier has no recurring bookings. Regulars keep their usual weekly slot only if staff book them before the Thursday release. Millbrook still has a coordinator and books about 80 people a week. Its numbers are steady, from 118 to 111. Dock Street and Westgate lost their coordinators on 1 May, and bookings fell from 74 to 3 a week. 129 of 213 April regulars lost their slot, and 88% of them are now inactive. Quarry Lane also lost its coordinator, but it kept paper rosters and barely declined. So neither the app nor the staffing cut explains it alone. The background check does not explain it: 121 of the 123 who lapsed held a current check. Commonplate shows little sign of mattering, since only 2 callbacks mention another group. Satisfaction scores look like a symptom. Don't cancel RotaWeave, which costs $14k and wouldn't fix the cause. Don't suspend checks, because the county contract and insurer require them. Don't purge the roster. Instead, give the unused admin seat to a staff member or trained lead volunteer. Have them book regulars into their usual slots at Dock Street and Westgate. Phone lapsed regulars to offer their slot back, and review after 60 days. Plan for Quarry Lane's 6 October go-live. Confidence is fairly high.
